recommendation_summary: The reply recommends wrapping the `nightly-sync` cron call so that a failure or timeout sends an alert, either by mailing on a non-zero exit or with a healthchecks.io dead-man's-switch ping, and building no Docker or logging stack.

labels.Requirements and who asked: you asked for "find out automatically if the job died." Nobody has asked for log aggregation, retention, search, or Docker as capabilities — that's solving a different problem (visibility into job internals) than the one that bit you (silent total failure).
labels.Deleted: central/Dockerized logging stack (Loki, ELK, Dozzle, etc.) on the Synology. It adds a service to run and watch, and still wouldn't have alerted you — it only helps once you're already looking.
labels.Bottleneck: `nightly-sync` has zero failure signal today; it only speaks on success. That's the single point to fix.
labels.Checked myself: this is from what you told me (cron time, crash point, four silent nights) — I haven't read the script or crontab.

note: The reply recommends one failure alert and gives two interchangeable ways to build it; the 'Requirements' line puts a paraphrase in quotation marks as if the user had said it, but it is still specific to this case.
